question: Explain the territorial and extraterritorial application of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 under Section 1.
modelAnswer: Under Section 1, the Sanhita applies territorially to every person for any act or omission contrary to its provisions committed within India. It also applies extraterritorially to: (a) any citizen of India committing an offence in any place beyond India; (b) any person on any ship or aircraft registered in India, wherever it may be; and (c) any person, anywhere, committing an offence targeting a computer resource located in India. The word 'offence' for this purpose includes any act done outside India which would be punishable if done in India. A savings clause preserves laws on mutiny/desertion in the armed forces and any special or local law.

question: When does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 come into force?
modelAnswer: Under Section 1(2), the Sanhita comes into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint by notification in the Official Gazette, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Sanhita.

question: What is the significance of Section 2 of the BNS?
modelAnswer: Section 2 is the definitions clause. It fixes the precise meaning of the key terms used throughout the Sanhita — such as 'dishonestly', 'fraudulently', 'document', 'good faith', 'public servant' and 'movable property' — so that these words carry a consistent meaning across every chapter, unless the context otherwise requires. Because definitional questions are asked independently of any specific offence, these terms are best studied as a glossary.

question: State the rule on the criminal responsibility of children under the general explanations in Chapter I.
modelAnswer: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age. Further, nothing is an offence done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve years of age who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion. Thus, a child under seven has complete immunity, while a child between seven and twelve has qualified immunity depending on maturity.

question: What new dimension of extraterritorial application does BNS Section 1 add compared to the earlier law?
modelAnswer: BNS Section 1 expressly extends the code to any person, in any place beyond India, who commits an offence targeting a computer resource located in India. This explicitly brings cross-border cybercrime affecting Indian systems within the reach of the Sanhita — a modernisation reflecting contemporary crime that the older provisions did not spell out as clearly.

question: Distinguish between 'dishonestly' and 'fraudulently' as defined in Section 2 of the BNS.
modelAnswer: Under Section 2, a person acts 'dishonestly' when he does an act with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another — the focus is on wrongful gain or loss of property. A person acts 'fraudulently' if he does a thing with intent to defraud, i.e. with deceit coupled with an intention to cause injury; it need not involve gain or loss of property. In short, 'dishonestly' centres on wrongful gain/loss, while 'fraudulently' centres on deceit and intent to defraud.

question: What is the meaning of 'good faith' under Section 2, and why is it significant?
modelAnswer: Under Section 2, nothing is said to be done or believed in 'good faith' which is done or believed without due care and attention. Its significance lies in the standard it sets: honesty alone is not enough — a person must act with reasonable care and attention. This definition matters across the code because many defences and exceptions depend on whether the accused acted in good faith.

question: Explain the general explanations in Section 3 regarding illustrations and the general exceptions.
modelAnswer: Section 3 explains that the 'General Exceptions' apply throughout the Sanhita even where a particular penal provision does not repeat them — so every offence must be read subject to those exceptions. It also clarifies that an illustration attached to a section is meant to help explain the provision but does not limit or exhaust its scope. These rules ensure the code is read consistently and that exceptions and explanatory illustrations operate uniformly across all chapters.
